Subject: Frostline inference follow-up: SLO priorities, topology options, and next steps

Hi Ava / Derek —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive: 

Top-level pain points you shared
- Latency spikes during peak hours affecting real-time triage workflows (~300-800ms currently).
- Cost unpredictability from ad-hoc burst loads.
- Compliance: data residency + per-request audit logs for PHI-sensitive payloads.

Goals you confirmed
- P95 inference latency < 200ms for short (<=512 token) model calls for triage use case.
- Steady-state throughput ~60 reqs/s with 30% headroom for bursts to 150 reqs/s.
- Deterministic cost per-1k tokens for budgeting and procurement.

Model / workload notes (from call)
- Primary model family: transformer-based open models in the 13B-70B range; prefer quantized variants if quality holds.
- Mix of short real-time calls (triage) and longer generation (note summarization, 1–2k tokens).
- Expect KV-cache reuse for conversational flows.

Initial topology options we discussed
1) Dedicated pool (recommended for predictable latency): reserved GPUs, autoscale policies for burst, private VPC peering for PHI.
2) Hosted + fallback routing: cheaper hosted model for non-critical paths with automatic fallback to dedicated when latency or SLOs at risk.
3) Private on-prem for regulated sub-set (if procurement requires).

What we will bring to the technical deep-dive
- A short SLO cost/throughput sketch (Excel) with batch sizing and quantization impact. (attached)
- A 1-page topology sketch showing routing, KV-cache placement, and audit-log flow. (attached)
- A checklist of questions for your infra/security team (data residency, KMS, access patterns).

Proposed next steps
- Technical deep-dive: Wed May 21, 10:00–11:00 PT (please confirm attendees).
- Derek: please share 1) a sample traffic profile (per-minute qps for past 2 weeks) and 2) any model-size preference.
- Purchasing: we will prepare a high-level estimate and an initial procurement checklist after the deep-dive.

Attaching: frostline_slo_calc.xlsx, redwood_topology_sketch.pdf

If any of the recap items above are off, flag them and I will update. Otherwise I’ll lock the deep-dive invite and our engineering leads will prepare the topology options with rough cost buckets.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez

Hi Ava / Derek — looping in more technical detail ahead of Wed’s call. I’ve annotated the attached Excel with sample calculations; highlights below.

Short summary (tl;dr)
- For triage (<=512 tokens) using a quantized 13B model we estimate: p95 ~ 120–180ms with 4-8 token batching and a warmed KV-cache; p50 ~ 45–70ms.
- For 70B distilled summarization (2k tokens) expect p95 in the 900ms–1.8s range depending on quantization level and batch packing; recommend async batch lanes for those jobs.

Sizing and topology recommendation (detailed options)
A) Dedicated-Pinned (recommended for P95 predictability)
  - Reserved V100/A100-equivalent GPUs in a private pool.
  - Autoscale policy: maintain baseline to handle 70% of steady-state; scale for 30% burst headroom.
  - Local KV-cache per-serving node + shared prefix cache at the routing layer to reduce cross-node misses.
  - Typical outcome: consistent p95 under 200ms for triage with predictable cost model.

B) Hosted + Fallback Routing
  - Primary: hosted Redwood-optimized quantized model for cost-efficiency.
  - Fallback: route to Dedicated when latency SLO breaches or sudden spike.
  - Useful when you want to keep most traffic on hosted but guarantee critical workflows.

C) Private-VPC (EU residency)
  - Private control plane deployed in your EU tenancy / VPC; audit logs pushed to your SIEM via secure syslog.
  - Integration with your KMS for request-level encryption keys.

Batching / Cache knobs we will validate on the call
- Dynamic batching window: 5–15ms for low-latency path.
- KV-cache TTL and prefilling strategy for conversation reuse.
- Quantization profile: 8-bit vs 5-bit (quality vs perf trade-offs) — we included sample BLEU-like quality deltas in the sheet.

Open questions for Derek (please prepare)
- Expected concurrency (p95) across triage endpoints during peak 1-hour windows.
- Token distribution: percent of calls <=512 tokens vs >512.
- Any hard limits on disk retention or on-prem archive requirements.

Attachments: frostline_slo_calc.xlsx (annotated) and redwood_topology_sketch.pdf

I’ll present the Dedicated vs Hosted+Fallback cost buckets in the deep-dive and run through the KV-cache architecture. Sergio — I put a short draft of an ops runbook in slide notes that we can turn into a mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Grace O’Connor
Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
